summary: Feed s079_single is degraded: 36.3% of TCP sessions (74/204) are one-way, breaking IDS stateful inspection. No duplicates, drops, overload, VLAN or encryption issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding only one direction for 36.3% of TCP sessions. Traffic likely traverses asymmetric paths captured on separate TAP/SPAN ports that are not aggregated to this single IDS feed, or a flow-hash load-balancer is splitting client->server and server->client to different tool ports. IDS therefore sees SYN/data one way without return traffic.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP state tracking, stream reassembly and signature matching. One-way flows prevent handshake validation, payload reassembly and bidirectional signature detection, causing missed exploits, C2 and incomplete session logging.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same IDS tool port using symmetric flow hashing so the IDS receives complete bidirectional sessions for stateful detection.
